text: The downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem states that:
choices: every finite theory has an infinite model
if a countable theory has a finite model, it has a countable model
if a countable theory has an infinite model, then it has a countable (infinite) model
every theory with an uncountable model has a largest model
explanation: Downward Löwenheim–Skolem: a countable theory with an infinite model has a countable model, built as a countable elementary substructure via Skolem functions. Option B misstates the hypothesis (it requires an infinite model); options A and D are unrelated fabrications. The upward direction, by contrast, yields models of every larger infinite cardinality.
